subtype: Fearful and alarmed in unsafe situations [Interpreting]
passage: Kunal was walking home along the canal path after the evening bus dropped him at the edge of the village. It was dusk, and a man on a motorbike had passed him twice, slowing each time. Samir's chai stall was a few minutes ahead, lit with a single bulb. Kunal's stomach tightened, and his steps got faster without his deciding. He didn't know if the man meant anything. Maybe he was lost. But Kunal decided not to wait to find out. He turned toward the stall and asked Samir for tea, standing near the bench where two old men sat. When the motorbike passed again, it didn't slow. Kunal waited a while, then asked Samir to walk with him to the main road.

qa.q: Where did Kunal buy tea?
qa.a: He bought tea at Samir's chai stall.

qa.q: What was Kunal feeling on the canal path, and did he treat it as proof?
qa.a: He felt uneasy, with a tight stomach, but he did not treat it as proof, noting the man might be lost.

qa.q: What steps did Kunal take that a wise person might copy?
qa.a: He moved toward a lit public place, stayed near other people, and asked Samir to walk with him.

qa.q: How might Samir have seen Kunal's request?
qa.a: Samir probably saw a neighbour who wanted company and likely agreed without any fuss.

grounding: Kunal notices a gut sense of danger, treats it as a cue, and moves to a public place and asks for help.

subtype: Fearful and alarmed in unsafe situations [Interpreting]
passage: Javier was leaving the library in Rotterdam at ten when he realised the same man had been behind him on two different streets. The man kept a few steps back and looked at his phone whenever Javier glanced round. Javier's mouth went dry. It might be nothing, he told himself, but his gut wouldn't settle. He crossed to a brightly lit takeaway, went in and stood near the counter. The man walked on. Javier texted Chen, "Can you meet me here? Feeling a bit weird." Chen arrived in ten minutes and they walked home together. Javier told the shop worker thanks. He decided to mention it to the campus security in the morning, in case others noticed the same thing.

qa.q: What time did Javier leave the library?
qa.a: He left the library at ten.

qa.q: What was Javier worried about when his mouth went dry, and did he treat the feeling as proof?
qa.a: They told him something might be wrong, but he admitted it might be nothing while still choosing to act carefully.

qa.q: What other step could Javier take beyond going into the shop?
qa.a: He could tell campus security, as he planned, and keep a friend informed of his route.

qa.q: How might Chen have felt when he got the text?
qa.a: Chen probably felt concerned and glad to be asked, since he came within ten minutes and walked home with Javier.

grounding: Javier feels a gut sense of danger, moves to a public place, asks a friend for help and reports it.

subtype: Fearful and alarmed in unsafe situations [Interpreting]
passage: At the university library in Kolkata, Tanuja stayed till the 10 p.m. closing bell. On the stairs she noticed a man she'd seen by the shelves earlier, now behind her. When she slowed, he slowed. When she turned onto the dark path to the hostel, his footsteps turned too. Her stomach knotted and her skin prickled. Maybe he was just a student going the same way. But she didn't wait to find out. She turned back towards the lit entrance, where the security guard sat, and stood by his desk. She texted her friend Damini: "Someone following me from library. At security desk." Damini replied within seconds: "Stay there, coming with Mona." The guard looked up. "Everything okay, madam?" Tanuja told him. The man walked past slowly and went towards the main gate. The guard noted the time, and Damini arrived and walked her back to the hostel.

qa.q: Where did Tanuja go when she felt followed?
qa.a: Back to the lit entrance, by the security guard's desk.

qa.q: What was Tanuja feeling on the dark path?
qa.a: She was afraid and uneasy, her stomach knotting and skin prickling, though she knew he might just be going the same way.

qa.q: What steps did Tanuja take that were sound?
qa.a: She moved to a lit place with a guard, texted a friend, told the guard, and walked back with company.

qa.q: How did Damini respond to Tanuja's message?
qa.a: Damini replied within seconds, told her to stay there and came with Mona to walk her back.

grounding: Shows a young adult treating a gut sense of being followed as a cue, moving to a public place and asking for help.

subtype: Fearful and alarmed in unsafe situations [Interpreting]
passage:
Dear Salma,
Something happened at the station yesterday and I want to tell you, because you always tell me to trust my gut.
A man came up to me near the ticket counter, very friendly, and said he had a job for me: "Data entry, great pay, start today." He kept standing too close, and when I said I'd think about it, he said, "Only today. My car is outside. Come now, don't tell your family, they'll just worry." Everything in my body went cold.
Maybe he was just a pushy recruiter. I don't know. But "now" and "don't tell your family" made my heart race. I walked straight to the railway police booth and told the constable. She took down his description and said I'd done the right thing. Then I called Ammi.
I'm fine. Just shaken. I'm telling you so you know the signs too.
Santosh

qa.q: Where did Santosh go after the man's offer?
qa.a: Straight to the railway police booth.

qa.q: How did Santosh feel when the man said "don't tell your family"?
qa.a: Santosh felt alarmed and scared, going cold with a racing heart, and was left shaken afterwards.

qa.q: What did Santosh do that was wise?
qa.a: Santosh treated the unease as a warning cue, left the man, reported it to the railway police and told family.

qa.q: How did the constable respond to Santosh's report?
qa.a: She took down the man's description and said Santosh had done the right thing.

grounding: Shows a young adult noticing pressure and a gut sense of danger, and leaving and reporting rather than going along.

subtype: Fearful and alarmed in unsafe situations [Interpreting]
passage: Akash, you asked for the scariest night of my college life, for your podcast. I'm Zubin. It was after a birthday party at a farmhouse outside the city. Around one, a senior I barely knew, clearly drunk, jangled his keys and said, "Come, I'll drop you. Everyone's leaving." Two others were already getting in. Something in my gut said no. His eyes were glazed, he was swaying, and when I hesitated he got angry. "What, you don't trust me?" My hands went cold. I made an excuse about waiting for a friend, walked back inside to where the host's mother was sitting, and told her. She took the keys off him, called cabs for all of us and made everyone wait in the living room. I still don't know if I was right about everything. But leaving was right.

qa.q: Where was the birthday party?
qa.a: At a farmhouse outside the city.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling when the drunk senior got angry?
qa.a: Zubin felt afraid, hands going cold, with a strong gut sense that getting in the car was unsafe.

qa.q: What steps did Zubin take that were sound?
qa.a: Zubin made an excuse, went back inside to a responsible adult and told her, instead of getting in the car.

qa.q: How did the host's mother respond when Zubin told her?
qa.a: She took the keys, called cabs for everyone and made them wait inside.

grounding: Shows a young adult treating a gut sense of danger as a cue and choosing to leave and ask for help.

subtype: Fearful and alarmed in unsafe situations [Interpreting]
passage: I run the chemist's shop by the bus stop, and I'm open till eleven. Last Thursday, around ten, a young woman came in fast and stood close to the counter, not looking at the shelves. Seema, I learned later. She kept glancing at the glass door. Outside, a man in a grey jacket had stopped under the streetlight, pretending to read his phone. He'd walked past twice already. Seema said quietly, "I think he's been following me from the station. Can I wait here?" I can't say he was following her; he might have been waiting for someone. But she looked frightened, and her hands were shaking on her bag strap. I said, "Stay as long as you like," and pulled a stool round. She called her friend Kiran, who said they'd come on the scooter in ten minutes. I also rang the beat constable, whose number I keep by the till. By the time the constable walked up, the man in grey had gone. Kiran arrived, and they left together.

qa.q: Until what time is the chemist's shop open?
qa.a: Till eleven.

qa.q: What was Seema feeling when she came into the shop?
qa.a: Seema felt frightened and alarmed, sensing she was being followed, with shaking hands and eyes on the door.

qa.q: Which of Seema's steps were sound?
qa.a: Moving into a lit public shop, asking to wait there, and calling a friend to come, while the shopkeeper rang the beat constable.

qa.q: How did the shopkeeper read the situation?
qa.a: The shopkeeper was unsure whether the man was really following her, but took her fear seriously enough to let her wait and call the constable.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult treating a gut sense of being followed as a cue, moving to a public place and asking for help, while the danger itself stays uncertain.
